issues.legal_issue: A candidate who acquired the required property before the application deadline satisfies the property eligibility requirement even if the ownership record is updated afterward.
material_facts: The candidate acquired agricultural land under a gift deed before the last date for submitting applications.
The land was entered in the revenue records after that deadline.
The candidate was treated as ineligible because the entry had not been made by the deadline.
issues.conclusion: The candidate possessed the land by the relevant deadline and was eligible; the later mutation entry did not alter that result.
issues.legal_principle: Under Rekha Chaturvedi v. University of Rajasthan, a candidate must possess the required qualification by the application deadline or other specified date. Applying Sawarni v. Inder Kaur, a mutation entry neither creates nor extinguishes title or ownership; acquisition of property and its entry in revenue records are distinct matters.

predicates.appointment_selection_appeal: The proceeding challenges a decision made in selecting or appointing a candidate.
predicates.property_acquired_before_cutoff: The candidate acquired the required property before the deadline for applications or other relevant qualification date.
predicates.mutation_recorded_after_cutoff: The property's entry in the revenue records was made after that deadline or relevant qualification date.

issues.definition: When a selection appeal concerns property eligibility, a candidate who acquired the required property before the relevant cutoff meets that requirement even if the revenue record was updated later.

issues.legal_issue: Examination marks may determine comparative merit when the governing selection direction makes them relevant and candidates satisfy the minimum eligibility requirements.
material_facts: Both candidates had passed the required school examination.
The governing departmental direction treated examination marks as the basis for selection, subject to minimum property and income requirements.
The candidate who was not appointed had obtained more marks than the appointed candidate.
The appointed candidate was preferred on the ground that the other candidate lacked property, although that candidate had acquired it before the application deadline.
issues.conclusion: The candidate who had higher marks was more meritorious, and the authorities had wrongly ignored her case.
issues.legal_principle: The notification required passing the school examination and gave no weight to higher educational qualifications. The departmental executive direction stated that selection should be based on examination marks, provided the candidate had the prescribed minimum property and income. A candidate meeting the minimum eligibility requirements could therefore be preferred on the basis of higher marks.

rule.if: appointment_selection_appeal and candidates_meet_minimum_eligibility and governing_selection_rule_uses_marks and candidate_has_higher_marks

predicates.appointment_selection_appeal: The proceeding challenges a decision made in selecting or appointing a candidate.
predicates.candidates_meet_minimum_eligibility: The candidates being compared satisfy the minimum requirements for the post.
predicates.governing_selection_rule_uses_marks: The applicable selection direction makes examination marks relevant to comparative selection, subject to minimum eligibility requirements.
predicates.candidate_has_higher_marks: The candidate whose selection is challenged obtained more marks in the relevant examination than the selected candidate.

issues.definition: Where candidates meet minimum eligibility and the governing selection rule uses examination marks, the candidate with higher marks has the selection preference.

issues.legal_issue: A tribunal may direct appointment of an eligible, more meritorious candidate whose case was wrongly ignored in the selection.
material_facts: The candidate challenging the selection was eligible by the application deadline and had obtained more marks than the appointed candidate.
The authorities ignored the candidate's application because they incorrectly treated a later revenue-record entry as proof that she lacked the required property.
The tribunal directed that the candidate be appointed, and the High Court upheld that direction.
issues.conclusion: The direction to appoint the eligible and more meritorious candidate was not illegal or unlawful and was not disturbed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court upheld the tribunal's appointment direction in light of the candidate's eligibility, greater merit under the applicable selection criteria, and the authorities' unlawful failure to consider her. The applicable departmental direction made marks relevant to selection once the prescribed minimum property and income requirements were met.

rule.if: employment_selection_appeal and candidate_eligible and candidate_more_meritorious and authority_wrongly_ignored_candidate

predicates.employment_selection_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning a tribunal's decision in an employment selection dispute.
predicates.candidate_eligible: The candidate satisfied the requirements for the post by the relevant qualification deadline.
predicates.candidate_more_meritorious: The candidate ranked higher under the applicable comparative selection criteria than the person selected.
predicates.authority_wrongly_ignored_candidate: The selecting authority excluded the candidate for a reason that did not lawfully disqualify the candidate.

issues.definition: In an employment selection appeal, a tribunal may direct appointment when an eligible candidate ranked higher under the applicable criteria and the authority wrongly ignored that candidate.

issues.legal_issue: An incumbent's prolonged service does not defeat relief for a candidate who promptly challenged an unlawful selection and whose case was delayed in adjudication.
material_facts: The unsuccessful candidate approached the tribunal promptly after the appointment was made.
The tribunal's consideration of the challenge took time, during which the appointed candidate continued working for several years.
The tribunal granted relief to the challenger and also observed that the incumbent could be considered for a nearby vacancy if otherwise fit.
issues.conclusion: The incumbent's prolonged service did not warrant disturbing the relief granted to the timely challenger; the possibility of considering the incumbent for a nearby vacancy if fit did not change that result.
issues.legal_principle: The Court distinguished Rekha Chaturvedi v. University of Rajasthan, where relief was refused after a lengthy delay, because the candidate in this case had approached the tribunal promptly and the delay resulted from the pending proceedings. That delay should not prejudice the candidate who sought relief in time.

predicates.employment_selection_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning a tribunal's decision in an employment selection dispute.
predicates.challenger_filed_promptly: The unsuccessful candidate challenged the selection without delay after the appointment decision.
predicates.incumbent_served_during_adjudication_del: The selected candidate continued working while the challenge remained pending for adjudication.

issues.definition: When an unsuccessful candidate promptly challenges an employment selection and the incumbent serves during the resulting adjudication delay, that tenure does not bar relief for the challenger.
